clips.title: Run Temporal Server locally on Docker and Minikube
clips.why: You see that a Temporal server is several services in front of a database, which is exactly what we install on inf.
look: The production notes at the start: a real install needs a real database.
The containers that come up: the server, its database and the web UI.
Where the namespace and the UI address appear once it runs.
clips.after: On inf the same pieces are a Helm chart, an RDS Postgres and an internal UI address, installed once with retention and search attributes decided up front.

clips.title: Temporal in 7 Minutes - the TL;DR Intro
clips.why: A short look at the developer tools and the UI, where every run and its history can be inspected.
look: The UI lists runs and lets you open one run's full history.
Everything you see there comes from the history in the database.
clips.after: Our UI is temporal-ai-agents.rhinohealth.com, and the search box there takes the same JiraKey and Agent queries as the CLI.

practice.q: Write the query that finds every run for the ticket RH-1234.
practice.hint: The search attribute name, an equals sign and the value in double quotes.
practice.why: JiraKey is a registered Keyword field, so an exact match on the whole value finds every run that carries it.

practice.q: Which type should the search attribute Agent have?

options.why: Agent holds short exact values such as nova or cifix, compared as a whole.
Text is split into words for full-text search. That is for sentences, not IDs.

practice.q: Put the install of our Temporal on inf in order.
items: Generate the database password into Vault
Copy the password into the cluster with an ExternalSecret
Install the Temporal Helm chart with 128 history shards and the ai-agents namespace
Register Agent, JiraKey and RunKind with the post-install job
Start the orchestrator worker, which starts runs that carry those fields
practice.why: Each step needs the one before it: the chart needs the database and its password, and runs need the fields to exist.

practice.q: A test copy of our Temporal was installed with 64 history shards. Can you later change it to 128 to match production?

options.why: Every run is tied to one shard for its whole life, so the number cannot change after the first install.

options.text: No, the number is fixed at the first install
options.why: That is why the value is chosen once, carefully, and copied from the product's Temporal.

options.text: Yes, but only while no run is open
options.why: Closed runs are still stored in their shards until retention deletes them, so the number still cannot change.
